item.title: How Angelina Jolie's NGO offers free legal aid to kids
item.description: Kids in Need of Defense, co-founded by Angelina Jolie in 2008, assists unaccompanied children with legal representation. KIND ensures that these children receive psychosocial support and comprehensive services across the United States and Mexico. The organization has aided over 17,000 children by connecting them with pro bono attorneys who understand their cases. Many of these children have endured significant trauma and require specialized interventions.

item.title: An 11-year-old Texas boy sold 700 Pokémon cards and toys, raising $20k+ for heart disease research
item.description: In an inspiring display of generosity, Texas schoolboy Ryan Ragsdale, age 11, has successfully raised over $20,000 for charity through selling his toys and other items. Since the tender age of five, Ryan has organized fundraisers via the American Heart Association’s Kids Heart Challenge, contributing to children battling heart defects. His creative fundraising methods include selling Pokémon cards, unique hand-painted rocks, and a collection of jokes.

item.title: Madonna’s charity opened a children’s surgery centre in Malawi. It now does 2,000+ operations a year
item.description: Madonna's charity, Raising Malawi, has established the Mercy James Centre for Paediatric Surgery and Intensive Care in Malawi. This facility performs over 2,000 life-saving surgeries each year at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital. The centre not only conducts surgeries but also serves as a training site for local medical professionals. Raising Malawi is currently raising funds to expand services and hire more specialist staff.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Quint Pottinger, Kentucky farmer who uses autonomous tractors to save his 245-year-old family farm
item.description: Meet Quint Pottinger, an eighth-generation Kentucky farmer turning to autonomous tractors to protect his family’s 245-year-old farm. After three years of drought reduced crop yields to 100-130 bushels per acre, technology is helping the family plant 800 acres of crops and cover crops, offering new hope for the farm’s future while reducing labour demands.

item.title: Built in 1930 as an Illinois orphanage, a 17-bedroom property later became a family mansion
item.description: Transforming a historic orphanage from 1930 into a grand private home, this Illinois property spans an impressive 10,000 square feet with 17 bedrooms. Up for auction, it starts at a suggested bid of $975,000. Buyers can tailor the unfinished interiors to their preferences, while preserving the building's original architectural charm and enjoying additional outbuildings for diverse uses.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Celine Dion's former Florida mansion sells for $12.5 million after a $20 million listing
item.description: Celine Dion’s former Florida mansion in Jupiter has sold for $12.5 million in an off-market deal. Built for the singer in 1998, the waterfront property was sold by her for $9 million in 2002. The 14,750-square-foot luxury home features eight bedrooms, a private dock, a swimming pool and a lavish home theatre. It was listed for $20 million earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: A Georgia court vacated a $186,000 renovation default judgment, sending the dispute back to court
item.description: A Georgia appeals court has recently vacated a default judgment related to a home construction issue between Juan Ramirez and Big Sky Remodel. The court identified that the initial trial court lacked adequate jurisdiction over Big Sky owing to service failures. Moreover, it ruled that damages were wrongly awarded to Ramirez prior to settling any questions of joint liability.

item.title: Just Helping recycled 88,544 Xmas trees in 2026 and raised a record £1,885,915 for local UK causes
item.description: A charitable organization in the UK has triumphantly gathered 88,544 discarded Christmas trees, turning them into valuable products. This initiative raised £1.88 million for various local charities, breaking past records. The substantial involvement of volunteers during the collection phase contributed greatly, while the campaign fostered significant environmental progress by curbing carbon emissions. The charity envisions expanding its recycling efforts to cover more regions in the future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Since 2022, workers have turned an illegal dump in FDR Park into a 33-acre wetland with 7,000 trees
item.description: In South Philadelphia, a once-neglected dumping ground has been reborn as a thriving tidal wetland, nurturing local wildlife. This impressive restoration project earned the Governor’s Award for Environmental Excellence from Pennsylvania’s Department of Environmental Protection. Not only does it serve as a crucial natural flood management system for stormwater, but it also enhances biodiversity by drawing in a variety of birds and mammals.

item.title: A US court voided a 2021 West Virginia law banning judicial address leaks for lacking safety notices
item.description: A recent ruling by a federal appeals court has invalidated a West Virginia statute aimed at safeguarding the personal information of public officials. The court found the law contradictory to the First Amendment’s free speech guarantees. Unlike similar regulations in other states, West Virginia's law imposed penalties on information publishers without prior notification, raising concerns from industry advocates about its potential risks for journalists and businesses.

item.title: Do spiders dream? Researchers studying spiders have found sleep patterns resembling REM sleep
item.description: A recent study on Australian jumping spiders has uncovered that these creatures undergo unique sleep stages, reminiscent of REM sleep. The observed sleep patterns, characterized by distinct periods of stillness interspersed with muscle movements and eye twitches, suggest that spiders possess more advanced sleep mechanisms than previously believed. Future research aims to explore their natural sleeping behaviors, offering insights into the links between sleep and cognitive processes across species.

item.title: Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce’s gift helps feed Nashville families
item.description: Prior to their wedding at Madison Square Garden, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to various charities. One of the notable beneficiaries was The Store, a Nashville non-profit aimed at combating food insecurity. Due to rising food costs, The Store had paused the admission of new families prior to receiving the donation. The couple's charitable efforts supported 20 local and national organizations, reflecting their deep community ties.
